RFC9552-5.1-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Tagged units changed only by the package move: identifiers re-qualified with bgpls., comments re-pointed; producer bodies byte-identical modulo the writeTLV->WriteTLV and field-export renames (TLV code constants verified unchanged). RFC 9552 Section 5.1: "To compare NLRIs with unknown TLVs, all TLVs within the NLRI MUST be ordered in ascending order by TLV Type." Native whole-Link-NLRI proof: ls_export TestRFC9552NativeLinkTLVsCanonicalOrder / ...ReorderedSource (unchanged). Core descriptor units moved verbatim (package clause only): 260 precedes 261 for mixed families, and no descriptor combination descends.

RFC9552-5.1-2.note: rejudge 2026-09-30 (was wrong: the units asserted repeated 518 inside a Node Descriptor, which 5.2.1.4 forbids; those tags are removed under D-15 and the units kept untagged). Now proven on the one producer that repeats a Type: the two ls_export units emit two 259, two 260, two 261, two 262 and assert them ascending by Value, and that no longer same-type TLV precedes a shorter one. The Length key never differs within a Type on this producer (259/260 are 4 octets, 261/262 16), so the Length clause is met by construction and asserted as a tie; the Value clause is discriminated: judge break (Value comparison reversed) turns both units red, revert records observed red.

RFC9552-5.1-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge). Section 5.1's three ordering clauses are now all driven through enforceRFC7606: type (existing descending 257-before-256 unit), same-type Length (TLV 1234 lengths 3 then 2 discarded; 2 then 3 kept byte-identical) and same-type Value (equal lengths, bb bb then aa aa discarded; aa aa then bb bb kept). Each malformed case is otherwise well framed, so only the order trips, and the survivor beside it is kept. Records observed red on bgplsTLVOrdered.

Judge probes: skipping the withdraw when a replacement exists turned the add/remove unit red; routing AFI 16388 into Withdrawn Routes turned the wire unit red. RFC9552-5.2-7.note: c23: send side driven through AnnounceNLRIBatch: + a peer with (16388,71) negotiated gets one UPDATE whose MP_REACH_NLRI starts 40 04 47; - an IPv4-only peer gets no UPDATE and ErrNoPeersAcceptedFamily. Records: revert on AnnounceNLRIBatch both polarities, Negotiate for the capability negative (prose narrowed to what Negotiate asserts, matching its body). Judge targeted probe: removing nc.Has(batch.Family) from the family gate turned the negative red and left the positive green, so the gate itself is what the negative proves. Receive side (an unnegotiated peer sending Link-State NLRI) not driven; the HEAD advertise/negotiate positive in capability holds no record. Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c31 judge): only an RFC7752-3.2-1 tag line was added to the doc comment of both reactor units; bodies and this row's tags are unchanged, and the judge re-ran the family-gate overlay (`nc == nil || !nc.Has(batch.Family)` reduced to `nc == nil`): negative red, positive green. Enforced stands.

RFC9552-5.2.1-1.note: Rejudged all current tagged carriers against RFC 9552 Section 5.2.1: 'When configured, these auxiliary TE Router-IDs (TLV 1028/1029) MUST be included in the node attribute described in Section 5.3.1 and MAY be included in the link attribute described in Section 5.3.2.' Preserved IS-IS TestRFC9552ISISNodeRouterID and TestRFC9552ISISNodeCarriesBothRouterIDs assert exact per-node IPv4 and IPv6 values from native LSP TLVs 134/140. New OSPF TestRFC9552OSPFRouterIDsReachExporter installs one area-scope opaque-type-1 Router Address LSA per router, conforming to RFC 3630 Sections 2.1 and 2.4.1, and compares the complete native node TLV multiset and final encoded BGP-LS Attribute bytes from the registered exporter against independent literals. It catches omission, substitution, duplication and invented IPv6 IDs, closing the previous OSPF and final-attribute proof gaps. Read indexV2 scope guards, trafficEngineering, snapshot router-ID collection, encodeTopology, originateAttributes and send. The single-positive annotation is appropriate for this inclusion obligation. TestRFC9552OSPFAuxiliaryRouterIDsNotCollapsed is untagged robustness evidence only: multiple Router Address LSAs from one router violate RFC 3630's exactly-one-LSA condition and are not the conforming positive. This is a source-level judgment; new native discrimination observations remain Main's responsibility, and no fresh independent-peer run is claimed.

RFC9552-5.2.2.1-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, second pass after the coordinator's comment-only fix). RFC 9552 Section 5.2.2.1: "When used as a Link or Prefix Descriptor for IS-IS, the Bits R are reserved and MUST be set to 0 (as per Section 7.2 of [RFC5120]) when originated and ignored on receipt." Receipt: TestRFC9552ISISMTIDReservedBitsIgnoredOnReceipt builds IS-IS (Protocol-ID 2) Link and Prefix NLRIs with MT-ID 0x00E and R bits 0x0 vs 0xF; bgpls.ParseBGPLSLinkTLVs and ParseBGPLSPrefixTLVs (descriptor_info.go:74/:188, mask & 0x0FFF; reached from the NLRI JSON path) must yield the same MT-ID [14] and still decode the following descriptor (192.0.2.1, 192.0.2.0/24). Its doc comment now names those producers correctly, and the body is unchanged. Origination: ls_export TestRFC9552NativeISISTopologyReservedBits gives an IS-IS link topology 4096 (an R bit set), requires replace to error and no UPDATE to be emitted. Both clauses exercised at real producers.

RFC9552-5.2.3.1-1.note: Independent source rejudgment against complete RFC 9552 Section 5.2.3.1: ‘The OSPF Route Type TLV MUST be included in the advertisement when the type is either being signaled explicitly in the underlying LSA or can be determined via another LSA for the same prefix when it is not signaled explicitly (e.g., in the case of OSPFv2 Extended Prefix Opaque LSA [RFC7684]).’ Read both tagged tests and their producers. internal/plugins/ospf/rfc9552_bgpls_export_route_type_test.go::TestRFC9552ExtendedPrefixResolvesRouteType installs actual Router, Summary Network, AS External and NSSA LSAs plus an Extended Prefix LSA, then synchronously requests the live publisher snapshot. Ten cases assert exactly one opaque-marked extended advertisement for router 2.2.2.2 and the exact route type: underlying zero resolves to each of 1 through 6; explicit AS/NSSA classes each distinguish Type 1 from Type 2. The opaque provenance guard prevents a base prefix alone satisfying the test; NSSA in another area exercises the cross-bucket lookup. internal/plugins/ospf/bgpls_export.go::publishBGPLSLocked processes base LSAs before extensions; v2 dispatches Extended Prefix LSAs to extendedV2Prefix, which consumes v2PrefixRouteTypes results and publishes RouteType on the prefix. The exporter subscription in internal/component/bgp/plugins/ls_export/export_plugin.go forwards source snapshots to replace; export_state.go::replace calls encodeTopology, and reconcile forwards encoded routes. export_encode.go::encodeTopology copies RouteType into PrefixDescriptor.OSPFRouteType, whose encoder emits nonzero values as TLV 264. internal/component/bgp/plugins/ls_export/export_rfc9552_polarity_test.go::TestRFC9552NativeOSPFRouteType independently drives replacement/reconciliation and asserts exactly TLV 264 value 1 in the captured prefix NLRI. This composes two unit boundaries; the LSDB test does not itself inspect BGP wire bytes, and the exporter test does not exercise all six route types or a live BGP peer. The single-positive annotation is valid for this origination obligation, not an exemption for underlying zero or a receive-refusal assertion. The owned edit is an ordinary exhaustive comment in the fixture switch, outside the tag claim; it requires audit rejudgment but does not by itself change discrimination behavior or claim hashes. Stored producer-halt records were read, not replayed or independently freshness-verified. Concurrent producer changes are not attributed to this comment edit.

RFC9552-5.3.2.1-1.note: Rejudged all current tagged carriers against RFC 9552 Section 5.3.2.1: 'All auxiliary Router-IDs of both the local and the remote node MUST be included in the link attribute of each Link NLRI.' Preserved IS-IS TestRFC9552ISISLinkRouterIDs and TestRFC9552ISISLinkCarriesAllRouterIDs assert exact local/remote IPv4 and IPv6 inclusion and separately forbid swapped values. OSPF TestRFC9552OSPFRouterIDsReachExporter uses conforming single Router Address LSAs and pins both directed links' exact 1028/1030 values through complete encoded attributes. TestRFC9552OSPFRouterIDAbsenceReachExporter uses absent, MaxAge and unrelated-opaque local sources with a live remote control: it requires the remote ID to remain on the correct side and forbids invented local IDs, with roles reversed on the reverse link. TestRFC9552OSPFInterASRouterIDsReachExporter uses RFC 5392 type-6 Link TLVs in both permitted area/AS scopes, mandatory remote-AS and permitted simultaneous remote IPv4/IPv6 ASBR IDs, with no prohibited Link ID; it requires local 1028 and remote 1030/1031 in exact final bytes and detects contamination from an internal same-four-octet-ID router. Read indexV2, trafficEngineering, linkAttributes and exporter attribute producers; Remote.ASN == 0 correctly prevents internal-ID borrowing. Literal complete snapshots and final attribute equality catch missing, swapped, duplicate or invented IDs rather than merely accepting a parse. The untagged multi-LSA case is robustness evidence, not a conforming positive; untagged wrong-scope and mixed-body regressions support provenance without adding tagged covers. This is a source-level judgment; new native discrimination observations remain Main's responsibility, and the documented FRR ordinary/inter-AS collectors are not claimed freshly passed.

RFC9552-5.3.2.3-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Downgraded from enforced. RFC 9552 Section 5.3.2.3: "If a source protocol uses a metric width of fewer than 32 bits, then the high-order bits of this field MUST be padded with zero." The only tag, plugin ls TestRFC7752TEDefaultMetricZeroPadded, writes lsTEDefaultMetric{Metric: uint32} and reads the uint32 back: lsTEDefaultMetric is constructed only by decodeTEDefaultMetric and its WriteTo has no non-test caller, so the assertion cannot fail on any byte Ze originates. Ze originates TLV 1092 in internal/plugins/isis/bgpls_export.go (3-octet IS-IS TE metric widened) and internal/plugins/ospf/bgpls_export.go; the isis pair tagged RFC7752-3.3.2.3-1 drives that producer but is not tagged here. The {single-polarity} annotation argues from lsTEDefaultMetric.WriteTo, which is not a production encoder. Closing this needs the isis/ospf origination units tagged to this row.

RFC9552-5.3.2.3-2.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Downgraded from enforced. RFC 9552 Section 5.3.2.4: "IS-IS small metrics are 6 bits in size but are encoded in a 1-octet field; therefore, the two most significant bits of the field MUST be set to 0 by the originator." Both tagged units drive lsIGPMetric.WriteTo, which has no non-test caller (plugin ls attribute types are decode-side; nothing re-encodes them in production), so neither can fail on what Ze originates. The live originator is internal/plugins/isis/bgpls_export.go, which emits a 1-octet TLV 1095 from entry.DefaultMetricValue, masked to 6 bits at decode by internal/plugins/isis/packet/tlv_neighbours.go (narrowMetricValueMask); no tagged unit drives that path with the two high bits set at the source. The negative (width grows to 2/3 octets above 0x3F) also only exercises the unused encoder.

RFC 9552 Section 8.2.2: "A BGP-LS Attribute MUST NOT be considered malformed or invalid based on the inclusion/exclusion of TLVs or contents of the TLV fields (i.e., semantic errors), as described in Sections 5.1 and 5.3." Session proof: reactor semantic/framing-twin attribute units (unchanged). ls units: unordered and unexpected TLVs walk without error; a TLV length past the attribute end is ErrBGPLSTruncated.

RFC9552-8.2.2-9.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge). The two bullets the earlier note named are now driven through enforceRFC7606: MP_UNREACH_NLRI length sum (Total NLRI Length 255 with 21 present: session reset + error, TestRFC9552LinkStateUnreachLengthOverrunResetsSession) and the sub-TLV length of a recognized TLV (TLV 256 framed at 8, sub-TLV 512 claiming 8 with 4 present: NLRI discarded, survivor kept). With the existing MP_REACH sum, TLV overrun, ordering and duplicate sub-TLV units and the well-formed negative, every concrete bullet of the section 8.2.2 list is driven; the 'per RFC 7606' bullet is the umbrella of the others.
